tip_title: Someone Gets Hurt at Your House. What Actually Happens With Your Insurance?
topic: Personal Liability Coverage - Injury on Your Property Scenario
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Someone Gets Hurt at Your House. What Actually Happens With Your Insurance?**

Fall is here, which means football watch parties, backyard hangs, and more people coming through your front door. Most homeowners know their policy has liability coverage, but fewer actually know how it works when someone gets hurt on the property. Your personal liability coverage pays for things like medical bills and legal costs if a guest is injured and you're found responsible, up to whatever limit is listed on your declarations page. The thing is, that limit was probably set when you first bought the policy, and it may not reflect how much you actually have to lose today. Standard limits start at $100,000, but experts generally recommend at least $300,000 for most households. If you're hosting regularly this fall, it's worth a quick look.

Not sure what limit you're carrying right now? Your Peachy agent can pull it up and walk through whether it still makes sense for you.

📖 [Learn more from U.S. News](https://www.usnews.com/insurance/homeowners-insurance/personal-liability-insurance)
